Run this once after you upgrade from version 0.x. It brings your old data into the new database.

## CLI: gournal migrate

Import the old entries.json file into the database, or apply a reviewed migration plan.

```text
gournal migrate [options]
```

### Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--plan <file>` | Apply this reviewed migration plan (a JSON file). |
| `--dry-run` | Compute the changes and write nothing. Needs --plan and --diff. |
| `--diff <file>` | Write the dry-run diff (Markdown) to this file. Needs --dry-run. |

## Examples

### CLI

Import the old `entries.json` file. This example ran in a journal folder that holds a 0.x `entries.json` with two entries. The first line is a note that gournal prints when it opens the folder. The second line is the result of the command.

```console
$ gournal migrate
gournal: imported 2 entries from entries.json
Imported 0 entries (2 already present).
```

Run the command again. The entries are already in the database.

```console
$ gournal migrate
Imported 0 entries (2 already present).
```
